title: Reliable CUDA-graph fragmentization and deterministic replay heuristics for multi-stream decode
creator: Ava Park
description: Investigate and implement a fragment-based CUDA-graph capture and deterministic-replay strategy that improves capture stability across heterogeneous decode streams and ensures correctness when falling back from graph replay to eager kernels. Deliver a heuristic layer that chooses fragment boundaries and kernel variants based on runtime signal (sequence-length distribution, KV cache hit patterns, device memory pressure) and a compact synchronization protocol to avoid inter-stream races during capture/replay cycles.
background: We regularly observe transient miscaptures and subtle token-atomicity regressions when graph capture spans multiple concurrent decode streams, especially on nodes with mixed sequence-length workloads and prefill/decode interleaving. Existing monolithic graph captures are brittle: a single unexpected prefill alignment change can invalidate replay, causing either incorrect outputs or falling back to inefficient eager execution. Prior tickets have focused on capture stabilization (ENG-82745, ENG-78921) but we still see nondeterministic replay failures under heavy co-tenancy and when kernel selection changes between capture and replay (different fused-attention vs strided kernels).
goals: 1) Create a deterministic, fragmentized graph capture model that isolates prefill and decode boundaries and tolerates incremental kernel variant changes. 2) Implement a heuristic classifier to choose fragment boundaries at safe alignment points (KV epoch boundaries, end-of-prefill tokens, attention-head stability windows). 3) Provide a lightweight replay verification pass that catches semantic divergence early and triggers safe fallback with minimal latency impact. 4) Add monitoring and alerts for capture fragility and replay fallbacks.
non_goals: Rewriting the entire kernel selection engine or replacing CUDA-graphs with an alternative capture mechanism in this ticket. Deep changes to scheduling across nodes (cross-node orchestration) is out of scope.
proposal: - Split captures into small, quiescent fragments anchored on prefill/dynamic-KV epoch boundaries. Each fragment records: the kernel variant used, input token offsets, and a short deterministic fingerprint (hash of key model dynamic shapes and first n tokens). - During replay, validate fragment fingerprints and kernel-variant compatibility before enqueueing the graph. - If compatibility mismatch detected, re-run fragment in eager mode and capture a replacement fragment asynchronously when stable. - Use stream-priority and CUDA events to serialize fragment handoffs; prefer fence-based handshake between prefill stream and decode stream to ensure KV cache visibility. - Add a lightweight in-memory fragment manifest per-serving-worker with epoch counters to defend against stale replay across process restarts.
design_details: - Fragment boundary selection heuristics: (1) End-of-prefill token positions (most stable), (2) KV cache epoch boundaries (after a prefix flush or cache-merge), (3) sequence-length cohort boundaries (group short vs long sequences to avoid branch divergence). - Kernel variant tagging: attach a compact tag for attention implementation (FUSED_V1, FUSED_V2, STRIDED, MATMUL_FALLBACK) and quantization profile (FP16, Q4, Q2). - Capture handshake: producer (prefill) stream triggers a CUDA event on completion; consumer (decode) stream waits on that event before starting dependent fragment capture. This avoids race conditions where KV writes are not visible. - Replay verification: replay fragment into a shadow workspace using deterministic RNG seed and compare first token logits against an eager fallback threshold (Linf < epsilon or KL divergence < tau). If divergence > threshold, mark fragment as invalid and execute eager fallback. - Fragment lifecycle: valid -> warmed -> stale; stale fragments are garbage-collected after N successful replacements or time T. - Fallback policy: single-token fallback allowed inline; sustained mismatches trigger immediate eager execution of the whole request to preserve correctness.
implementation_steps: Add fragment manifest data structures to serving-worker memory with lightweight indexing by (model_version, worker_epoch, fragment_id)
Implement boundary detector that observes batch token distributions and emits candidate fragment start/end markers
Instrument kernel-launch path to attach variant tags to captured graphs and persist to manifest
Add CUDA event handshake primitives in prefill and decode paths and unit tests for visibility ordering
Implement replay verifier that runs a micro-replay and compares logits/softmax fingerprints with configurable thresholds
Add async fragment recapture path that runs replacement capture in background and swaps manifest entry atomically
Expose telemetry: fragment capture rate, replay pass/fail counters, fallback latency heatmap
Integrate with rollout: feature flag guarded behind runtime-config and default off for existing clusters
testing_plan: Unit tests for fragment manifest CRUD and recovery after worker restart
Deterministic integration tests: synthetic multi-stream workloads with known prefills to validate no inter-stream races
Fuzz tests that randomly change kernel variants mid-capture and assert safe fallback behavior
Performance benchmarks comparing monolithic capture vs fragmentized capture on mixed-seq workloads (latency p50/p95, token throughput)
Canary rollout on small fleet with increased assertion-level logging and auto-roll back on >0.5% regression in successful-response-rate
observability: - New dashboard panels: fragment_capture_rate, fragment_replay_success_rate, fragment_fallback_rate, avg_fallback_latency. - Alert: fragment_fallback_rate > 0.3% sustained for 5m -> P1. - Traces: attach fragment_id and kernel_tag to decode traces for root-cause analysis. - Sampling: capture full logits diff for 1% of fallback events for offline analysis.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge behind runtime-config flag. 2) Unit/integration tests green. 3) Internal canary: rollout to 5% of serving workers for 24h, monitor fallback_rate and latency. 4) Gradually increase to 50% over 72h if metrics stable. 5) Full rollout with gradual GC tuning. 6) Post-rollout: run a sampling job to verify long-tail correctness over 7 days.
risks: - Fragmentization may increase capture overhead if fragments are too small, raising per-token cost. - Replay verification adds extra work; misconfigured thresholds may cause unnecessary fallback. - Interactions with kernel autotuner could change kernel tags frequently, causing churn. - Race conditions during manifest swap could lead to stale fragment usage if atomicity is not enforced.
mitigations: - Start with conservative fragment sizes (prefer end-of-prefill boundaries) and tune with telemetry. - Expose threshold knobs and enable adaptive thresholds based on historical variance. - Wire kernel-tagger to prefer stable names and include version hashes; add hysteresis to prevent constant tagging churn. - Use atomic compare-and-swap when swapping manifest entries and add a durability write to local checkpoint on critical state transitions.
